text:
pagerduty-bot: P1 alert -> GPU pool 'gpu-pool-usw' reached autoscaler ceiling (max nodes) and request queue is growing > 15k. Throttling requests. Impact: generation latency >30s and 500+ errors. Pager: @mike_oncall

mike_oncall: seeing it. queue size 15.2k, avg wait 32s. Autoscaler shows max_nodes=80 and nodes=80, pods pending 120.

sara_ops: jumping in — are we able to increase max_nodes or is there a hard quota?

kevin_infra: current cloud quota for GPUs in us-west1 is soft 100; autoscaler cap was manually set to 80 by safety policy last month. We can request quota bump but that takes ~1h normally. Manual bump of autoscaler cap is possible but need approvals.

liz_prod: customers affected: two large enterprise jobs in prod (cust-A long-running chat, cust-B batch embeddings). Support tickets rising. We should call a bridge and notify CS.

eva_sre: can we temporarily evict low-priority pods/DRY-run scale? any cheap wins before manual cap raise?

mike_oncall: plan: 1) open bridgecall for immediate coordination 2) attempt safe manual cap raise to 100 nodes (pre-approved by infra leads) 3) if cap bump works, let queue drain and monitor errors 4) postmortem. anyone object?

sara_ops: fine. opening bridge now — joining bridge + recording.

sara_ops: Bridge link: https://meet.redwood/bridge/3371112223 (started). @kevin_infra pls join.

kevin_infra: on bridge. I've reviewed quota; cloud provider shows available headroom up to 120 but account limits might block provisioning >100. I can attempt autoscaler update to 100; if pods still pending we can consider manual immediate node provisioning.

mike_oncall: ok do autoscaler update. Put the command here when you run it. Also annotate with reason so audit logs are clear.

kevin_infra: running: ```
# increase autoscaler max for gpu pool
rwdctl autoscaler set-max --pool gpu-pool-usw --max-nodes 100 --reason "P1: queue growth and customer impact, manual emergency bump"
```

deploy-bot: Job queued -> applying autoscaler config change (change-id: c8f3a7b).

kevin_infra: change applied, cloud API accepted. Autoscaler max_nodes now 100. Starting provisioning of additional nodes.

mike_oncall: monitoring node launch and pod scheduling. kube events show nodes registering.

sara_ops: pods pending dropping from 120 -> 60 in the last 90s. Queue size dropping to 9.1k. latency median down from 32s -> 18s.

liz_prod: open CS note -> informing impacted customers that we are mitigating and will follow up with RCA. Copying key metrics into the ticket.

kevin_infra: a handful of pods still stuck due to image pull burst, added temporary increase to imagePullParallelism on registry. That cleared ~30 pods.

mike_oncall: good call. queue now 3.6k, errors reduced to ~40/min from peak 520/min. Working throughput back to nominal for most routes.

eva_sre: are there any persistent throttles at the request router layer that may keep failing even after capacity comes back? I'm seeing 429s from rate-limiter for long-tail clients.

mike_oncall: disabling catch-all short-term rate-limit for LLM-gen route for paid tiers to help backlog drain. Command: ```
rwdctl router update-rate --route /v1/generate --tier paid --limit 0 --reason "P1 backlog drain"
```

deploy-bot: Router policy update accepted.

sara_ops: after router change, 429s dropped to single digits, overall queue now sub-800 in 2m.

liz_prod: CS updated customers. One large customer (cust-A) confirm partial degraded UX but stable now. No data loss.

kevin_infra: note: cloud autoscaler metrics show node provisioning plateau at 96/100 due to AZ placement. I'm going to provision 4 smaller preemptible gpus in another AZ to reach desired capacity faster. Executing: ```
cloudctl compute instances create --pool gpu-pool-usw-azb --count 4 --gpu nvidia-a10 --preemptible --labels emergency-bump
```

mike_oncall: get that done and monitor for interruptions. Also leave audit trail.

kevin_infra: done. Instances live and joined cluster. Pods scheduled. Queue dropping under 200.

mike_oncall: we're back to normal-ish. I'll stay on bridge for 15 more minutes then handoff to follow-up track (postmortem & runbook). Any objections to closing the immediate incident?

eva_sre: thumbs. Recommend we keep autoscaler max=100 for 24h while investigating root cause and testing safer thresholds. Also create temp alert for queue >1k for 30m.

sara_ops: noted. Created alert: "gpu-pool-usw queue > 1k for 30m" (rule id: ALERT-3371).

liz_prod: logging customer impact summary: 3 enterprise customers saw degraded latency; 1 created a high-priority ticket; estimated lost requests ~1.2M tokens during peak. Sharing with AE and CS.

mike_oncall: next steps (action items):
- kevin_infra: confirm cloud quota and request permanent bump + update autoscaler safety policy (due EOD)
- eva_sre: triage and run evals to find hot prompts causing burst; add canary to detect similar workload patterns (48h)
- sara_ops: draft incident timeline + bridge recording (2h)
- liz_prod: customer comms follow-up + refunds/check credits for affected customers (ASAP)

kevin_infra: filing quota request now. Will ping when cloud confirms.

sara_ops: closing bridge now, leaving thread open for postmortem notes. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

mike_oncall: incident resolved for now. Keeping autoscaler max at 100 as agreed. Will open formal postmortem and link here.

pagerduty-bot: Incident resolved by manual autoscaler cap increase and emergency provisioning. Duration: 00:42:37.

mike_oncall: filing postmortem ticket: https://issues.redwood/INC-337111 — assign to eva_sre, kevin_infra, sara_ops.

sara_ops: attaching logs: ```
# quick capture
kubectl get pods -n inference --field-selector=status.phase=Pending
# autoscaler status
rwdctl autoscaler status --pool gpu-pool-usw
```

kevin_infra: note for postmortem: consider autoscaler policy change: soft ceiling should be dynamic based on cloud quota and AZ headroom. Also consider staged ramping rules to avoid sudden pod scheduling storms.

liz_prod: I'll coordinate customer exec notes once all metrics are finalized.

mike_oncall: great work. Closing active mitigation. Postmortem to be published within 72h.

sara_ops: thread locked to reduce noise, reply here for follow-ups.
